$comment: Golden cases for the MFC re-import (import.proto) and for an import write or conflict crossing a client's own edit (sync.proto rule 6, IMPORT CROSSINGS and IMPORT CONFLICTS). Every implementation (fc-coordinator's import and Push path, fc-mobile's store and sync engine) must agree with every case. `crossings`: one facet K on one client whose device is devices.self; each step is a Delta event (take), a user edit (edit), a Push of the unpushed edits (push), the PushResult of the oldest pushed edit (answer) or the user's resolution (resolve), and `expect` is the client after it: the value shown, the pending import conflict (MFC's side) or null, and the unpushed edits. Values stand for K's own fields; null is a tombstone. `keyedCrossings`: the same steps over several keys on one client, an origin facet's value standing for its MFC id and a conflict facet's for its `against`; `expect` gives the values shown for some keys, every pending import conflict (key: MFC's side) and the unpushed edits as [key, value]. `conflictPushes`: the server applying pushes to a key K that holds a pending import conflict; `now` is the server's clock, and `expect` is the outcome, K, the conflict facet ({against, version}) and whether it is pending. `reimports`: one import over abstract ids (occ ids order by name; new:{k} is the copy minted at ordinal k), heads (survivors maps a merged head to its survivor) and values. A figure cell is {value, v, base, baseV}: v and baseV rank versions, and this import writes at 100. `expect` is the whole state after the import, the user-owned and origin keys it wrote, the conflicts pending, and the unresolved rows.

crossings.name: an offline edit made before the import, the import write arriving by Delta first, is held and presented (S1)
the same edit pushed first and answered STALE with the import write is kept and presented, not adopted
an edit made after the import ran but before the phone saw it, already APPLIED, still presents the older import write (S2)
with the import write first, a newer unpushed edit is held, not pushed over it, until the user resolves (S2)
an import write equal to the edit crosses nothing
an import write the client had already taken, delivered again, crosses nothing
another device's write is ordinary LWW, not an import conflict
another device's write ends a pending import conflict, and the held edit then follows the ordinary rules
an import tombstone (MFC removed the copy) crossing an unpushed status edit is presented; taking MFC's side writes the tombstone
once the phone's own write has come back through Delta, a later import write is ordinary
an offline edit and its revert (5, 9, 5), unpushed, change nothing: they are dropped and the import write is taken
an edit and its revert made after the import ran (S2), unpushed, are dropped too, so the older import write is not pushed over
the same edit and revert already pushed cannot be recalled, so the import write is presented

keyedCrossings.name: GR-Q3 offline (S1): the phone sold o1 and the import, not seeing it, removed o2; the removal arriving first crosses the sale and is presented, and keeping the app's side writes o2 again
GR-Q3 offline (S1), the sale pushed first: APPLIED, since the import wrote no o1, and the removal arriving before its echo still crosses it; taking MFC's side removes o2
GR-Q3 offline (S1), the phone sold o2, the very copy the import removed: the removal crosses that copy's own sale
GR-Q3 offline (S1), the phone sold o2 and pushed first: answered STALE with the removal, which is held, not adopted
GR-Q3 (S2): the phone sold o1 after an import it had not seen removed o2; pushed and APPLIED, the older removal still crosses the sale
GR-Q3 (S2) with the removal first: the newer sale is held, not pushed over it, until the user resolves
raise (S1): the app added a copy offline and MFC raised the Count; the import's new copy crosses the app's addition, and keeping the app's side tombstones MFC's copy
raise (S2), the app's copy pushed first: added after the import and APPLIED, it still crosses MFC's new copy; taking MFC's side makes that copy live too
a sale taken back offline (owned, former, owned) changes nothing, so the removal of the other copy is taken
an import that changes another copy's kind removes and adds nothing, so it crosses no sale
an app copy of another kind, and a sale in another row, cross no addition
an import removal the client took before its sale, delivered again in a replay, crosses nothing
another device's write to the removed copy ends the row conflict, and the held sale is pushed
a conflict raised on a field the phone edited offline before the import (S1) is presented and the edit held; the resolution is minted above the conflict
a conflict raised on a field the phone edited offline after the import (S2), already pushed and APPLIED, is still presented: the user never saw it
a conflict the client had taken before its edit, delivered again, crosses nothing: that edit is the user's resolution

conflictPushes.name: an edit minted before the import that raised the conflict, pushed after it, lands but has not seen it: `against` moves to it and the conflict stays pending
the user's resolution, minted above the conflict facet's version, resolves it
an edit minted after the import but below the moved conflict facet has not seen it either, and keeps it pending
a push that loses by LWW changes nothing
an edit minted after the import that raised the conflict resolves it on the server; the phone that made it presents the conflict (keyedCrossings)
two older edits in turn each move `against`, and the resolution above the last move resolves it

reimports.name: an unchanged export writes nothing
a figure value changed only on MFC is written, with its base
a figure value changed only in the app is kept
a figure value changed alike on both sides moves only its base
a figure value changed differently on both sides is a conflict, and nothing is written
after a spine merge an unchanged export writes nothing, re-keys nothing and raises no conflict
after a spine merge a value MFC changed is written under the head its base was written under
after a spine merge a value the app deleted conflicts at the survivor, where the resolving write goes
GR-Q3: one of two owned copies marked former in the app and the Count lowered on MFC writes nothing; the other copy stays owned
MFC lowered the Count and the app changed nothing: the highest occ id is removed
MFC raised the Count: a new copy at the lowest unused ordinal
MFC raised the Count after an import removed a copy: that copy is restored, filing and all
the app added a copy and MFC raised the Count: the app copy is adopted, not duplicated
the app removed a copy (the highest, by PICKS) and MFC lowered the Count: nothing is written
the Count changed differently on both sides: a conflict per copy, and no status is written
MFC changed the kind and the app did not: the status is written and a filing of the old kind is reset
MFC and the app both marked the copy arrived: only the base moves
MFC marked the copy arrived and the app marked it former: a conflict on its status
MFC went from two ordered to one owned and the app had marked one arrived: the arrival is kept, the other copy removed
a row gone from the export removes the copies and figure values the app did not change
only MFC removed the copies, but the app changed some: the shortfall is raised as a conflict
Count 0 states no copies, and the row still states its figure values
a later row with the same canonical id is unresolved, and the first row stands
unresolved rows write nothing and leave their earlier copies and figure values alone
the spine now resolves the id to another figure (not a merge): unchanged heads follow, and so do the figure values
rows resolving to one survivor take its figure values from the numerically lowest MFC id
two rows' products merged after one import wrote both bases at one version: an unchanged export writes nothing, whichever head is listed first
two merged rows' bases at one version: MFC changed the row whose value is shown and no row states it now, so the numerically lowest row's value is written under the head shown (the lower head_id)
after a merge the more recent base stands, as long as a row still states it: an unchanged export writes nothing
